problem.statement: Tune hyperparameters and select models by repeatedly evaluating candidates on the same held-out test set, then report that test score as the final estimate of generalization.

approach.summary: Use the test set as the selection signal across many trials and quote its score as the final result.

failure.point: Each decision made using the test set leaks information about it; across many trials the reported score adapts to that particular set and overstates true generalization.
failure.evidence: Standard ML methodology (scikit-learn "Cross-validation" guidance; the adaptive-data-analysis literature, e.g. Dwork et al., 2015) prescribes a separate validation set or nested cross-validation for selection, leaving the test set untouched until the end.

transferability.notes: Applies whenever the same data drives both selection and final evaluation. A test set used exactly once, or nested CV, avoids it.

confidence.notes: Methodological failure; the bias is statistical and grows with the number of selection trials rather than being a single deterministic error.
